key_insight: FaceJev makes judgments about individual facial parts explicit learning targets for face forgery detection, rather than relying only on textual explanations. It uses a multimodal large language model to make direct visual decisions about facial plausibility.
problem_solved: Face forgery detectors often work well on familiar manipulation techniques but struggle with unseen ones. Existing MLLM-based approaches seldom explicitly train the individual facial-part judgments underlying their assessments.
method: Use a multimodal large language model to recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility.
Treat individual facial-part decisions as explicit learning targets instead of expressing judgments only through text.
Apply direct visual decisions to face forgery detection; further implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: Explicit facial-part supervision offers practitioners a direction for developing detectors that may generalize better to unfamiliar forgeries. The provided abstract does not include results confirming performance gains.
visual_elements: A face diagram highlighting individual regions with illustrative plausibility labels.
A pipeline showing face image → MLLM → facial-part decisions → forgery assessment.
A side-by-side comparison of textual explanations versus explicitly supervised visual decisions.
Icons contrasting familiar and unseen manipulation techniques to illustrate the generalization challenge.
paper_title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
paper_authors: Siran Peng, Tianshuo Zhang, Yibo Xue, Ajian Liu, Haoyuan Zhang
